🧭 Last week — media trends AI summary
Issue 1

⚔️ Escalation of Iran-US/Bahrain Strikes and Widening Hormuz-Gulf Conflict

Key summary
  • Earlier in the week, Iran launched an attack targeting US Patriot radar at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain, with the IRGC claiming it targeted US positions, triggering alert sirens across multiple areas of Bahrain.
  • Bahraini authorities confirmed a civilian industrial facility was hit and caught fire but reported no casualties. Separately, the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at western Saudi Arabia, indicating tensions are continuing simultaneously across the Gulf region.
  • US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confirmed he has been residing at a US military base for two weeks following an Israeli warning, exposing the continued high level of threat against senior US officials.

Issue 2

🤝 Possible Revival of Qatari Mediation and US-Iran Pursuit of a 'Permanent Deal'

Key summary
  • On November 21 (US time), President Trump said in a phone interview with Fox News that he would pursue a 'permanent' deal to prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons, stating he wants a binding agreement that remains in effect beyond his own term, while ruling out regime change.
  • Despite escalating armed conflict risks, including a tanker strike in the Strait of Hormuz, reports indicate that behind-the-scenes negotiation channels between the US and Iran remain active, drawing attention to whether Qatar—given its past mediating role—could help restart peace talks.

Issue 3

🇩🇪 Strengthening Qatar-Germany Strategic and Economic Cooperation (Amir's Visit and Economic Dialogue)

Key summary
  • The Amir of Qatar's visit to Germany highlighted the depth of the Qatar-Germany strategic relationship, followed by Qatar's Prime Minister and Foreign Minister jointly opening the 'Qatar-Germany Economic Dialogue' in Bonn with the Minister-President of North Rhine-Westphalia.
  • The Economic Dialogue serves as a high-level platform to expand bilateral cooperation in investment, technology, and industry, seen as part of Qatar's efforts to diversify its economic and diplomatic ties within Europe.
  • Separately, Qatar also participated in a technology and investment summit held in the United States, strengthening its global technology and investment networks, pursuing economic and diplomatic diversification with the West even amid regional military tensions.

Issue 4

💣 Continued Israeli Strikes and Humanitarian Crisis in Gaza Despite the 'Ceasefire'

Key summary
  • Even after the October 2025 'ceasefire' declaration, reports indicate that the Israeli military continues to destroy residential buildings in Gaza as part of a 'gradual forced displacement' policy, with the cumulative death toll since the ceasefire reaching 1,661 to 1,671 (including at least 9 deaths in the past 48 hours).
  • Following an Israeli targeted strike that killed three Gaza aid workers, Hamas called for an urgent international meeting, while Turkey criticized Israel for blocking thousands of container homes intended for entry into Gaza.

This page automatically collects and summarizes public news coverage and material from relevant institutions across Qatar, Iran, other major countries and Korea. News is gathered by querying Google News RSS feeds, Naver News search, and outlet RSS (Al Jazeera, BBC, etc.) with keywords such as Qatar, the Middle East and energy; in-depth reports are collected directly from the publication boards and RSS of domestic and international research institutes, international organizations and consultancies (supplemented by news search targeting those publishers), keeping only analyses and reports on the Middle East situation, the Iran war and their industrial, supply-chain and energy repercussions. The report list accumulates items published since the war's outbreak (2026-02-28), split into domestic and overseas and ordered by publication date (newest first). Collection and summarization rely on each outlet's publicly available headline and snippet; for subscription or paywalled outlets, the full article can be opened through the provided source link only after the reader signs in or subscribes to that outlet directly. The collected articles are automatically clustered and summarized by issue, and translated into English and Arabic, by Anthropic Claude (Sonnet 5) AI. The whole process runs and publishes automatically twice a day (07:00 and 15:30 Qatar time) via GitHub Actions. The Qatar government activity section separately curates only official statements, announcements and actions on the war and regional situation by Qatar government and state entities — the Emir, the Prime Minister, the ministries of Foreign Affairs, Defense and Interior, the Government Communications Office (GCO), QatarEnergy and the state news agency (QNA). Owing to automated collection some articles or reports may be missed, so please re-verify important issues against the original sources and further searches.
- Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Qatar, Commercial Section · KOTRA Doha
